meta.title: Who really said "Be yourself; everyone else is already taken"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: No, Oscar Wilde didn't say “Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.” It’s an anonymous modern saying first traced to a 1999 Usenet post.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Be yourself; everyone else is already taken'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Oscar Wilde. Quote Investigator traces this line to an anonymous 1999 Usenet post — the true author is unknown.

answer.label: Not Oscar Wilde — an anonymous modern saying
answer.sourceLine: There is no evidence Oscar Wilde said or wrote this. Quote Investigator ↗ finds the earliest exact match in an anonymous December 1999 Usenet post, with no author named; the line does not appear in Wilde’s works, and the Oscar Wilde Society calls it “definitely not Oscar.”

source.heading: The paper trail
source.excerpt: Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.
trail: Quote Investigator ↗ finds “no substantive evidence” Wilde said it and dates the earliest exact match to an anonymous December 1999 Usenet post.

A thematically related line — “there is very little chance of my being anybody else” — appears in Thomas Merton’s 1967 essay Day of a Stranger, per Quote Investigator ↗, but its wording and tone differ from the popular saying.
Check Your Fact ↗ quotes Oscar Wilde Society chairman Donald Mead — “This is definitely not Oscar” — and reports the line is absent from Wilde’s complete works.
source.excerptNote: Often printed as “Be yourself. Everyone else is already taken.” No documented source ties this exact wording to Oscar Wilde or to any named author.
source.rightsNote: The exact wording has no identifiable author or first-publication work — the earliest trace is an anonymous 1999 Usenet post — so no copyright status can be responsibly asserted. It is not a Wilde text and cannot be called public domain on that basis.

author.name: Oscar Wilde
author.heading: Why it lands on Wilde
author.bio: Oscar Wilde was an Irish writer whose plays and epigrams made him one of the most quotable figures in the English language — and, for that reason, one of the internet’s biggest magnets for invented quotations. His genuine celebrations of individualism make a feel-good line like this feel Wildean, which is exactly how fabrications get pinned to him. But feeling Wildean is not the same as being his.

cite.sourceCitation: Garson O’Toole (Quote Investigator), “Be Yourself. Everyone Else Is Already Taken,” QuoteInvestigator.com, Jan 20, 2014. Earliest documented exact wording: anonymous Usenet post, December 1999.

misattribution.heading: How it went Wilde
misattribution.intro: This is one of the internet’s most confidently mis-credited lines. It is stamped on posters, mugs, and social feeds as Oscar Wilde — but the trail leads nowhere near him.

items.why: The line appears in none of Wilde’s plays, essays, letters, or recorded conversation. Wilde Society chairman Donald Mead told Check Your Fact ↗: “This is definitely not Oscar. It is all over the internet with no source.”
Before Wilde’s name stuck, Quote Investigator ↗ notes the saying was credited around 2000 to an otherwise-unknown “Gilbert Perreira” — another unverifiable name.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest answer: the author is unknown. The earliest exact match is an anonymous December 1999 Usenet post, per Quote Investigator ↗ — the Wilde credit was added later with no evidence.

context.heading: Why it feels like Wilde
lead: The saying works as a Wilde quote because it flatters both the reader and the supposed author: it’s brisk, affirming, and lightly paradoxical — the shape of a Wildean epigram. Wilde really did prize individualism, which makes the fake feel plausible enough that few people check.
context.pull: Sounding Wildean is easy. Being Wilde is harder to prove — and here the proof is missing.
